mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes SL 350, 400 or 450 modern engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M276 engine for the SL 350 costs £3,200-£4,500 supply-only; a rebuilt M276 engine for the SL 400 or SL 450 costs £3,500-£5,500 supply-only. Fitting adds £1,200-£2,000 depending on complexity - modern V6 and turbocharged work requires specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain tensioner failure on a Mercedes SL 350, 400 or 450?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rattling noise on cold start lasting a few seconds is the classic warning sign on the M276 V6 engine. The hydraulic secondary chain tensioners can lose oil pressure, allowing chain slack. If ignored, it can lead to more serious engine damage.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes SL 350, 400 or 450 modern engine (M276) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M276 V6 is generally considered a reliable and well-engineered engine. It has minor common faults like oil leaks and problematic camshaft adjusters/cam followers, but it was so good that Mercedes put it in everything between 2010-2017. The M276 does not suffer from the balance shaft issues that plagued the earlier M272.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes SL 350, 400 and 450 modern engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M276 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work. Timing chain tensioner issues typically appear between 60,000-100,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes SL 350, 400 or 450 modern?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the SL is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt M276 costs £3,200-£5,500 - far less than replacing a £15,000-£40,000 vehicle. The R231 SL's strong residual values make engine replacement a justifiable investment.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes SL 350, 400 or 450 modern need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies MB 229.5 high-performance oil - typically 5W-30 or 5W-40 fully synthetic. The M276 V6 requires approximately 7.5-8.0 litres with filter.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz SL 350/400/450 Modern - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The R231 SL 350 launched in 2012 as the entry-level petrol SL, powered by the M276 3.5-litre naturally aspirated V6 producing 306hp. In 2014, the SL 400 replaced it with the M276 3.0-litre twin-turbo V6 delivering 333hp. In 2017, the SL 450 succeeded the SL 400 with a further-developed M276 biturbo V6 producing 367hp and paired with the new 9G-TRONIC 9-speed automatic transmission. These modern V6 engines represented a significant step forward in efficiency, power and refinement for the SL range.

milestones.description: M276.954, 3.5L naturally aspirated V6, 306hp @ 6,500rpm (SL 350, R231 launch)
9G-TRONIC 9-speed automatic transmission introduced across all models

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mercedes Benz SL 350, 400 and 450 modern is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points - from M276 timing chain tensioner rattle to M278 oil cooler seal leaks and carbon buildup on intake valves.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz SL 350/400/450 Modern Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The R231 SL 350, 400 and 450's M276 V6 engines are among Mercedes' most refined modern petrol units - smooth, powerful and generally reliable. However, they have well-documented weaknesses that can lead to significant repair costs. Timing chain tensioner rattle, oil cooler seal leaks, and carbon buildup are the most common issues driving replacement enquiries. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: M276 Timing Chain Tensioner Rattle - The Modern SL's Cold-Start Warning
problems.rootCause: The M276's hydraulic secondary chain tensioners can lose oil pressure over time, causing a metallic rattling noise on cold starts until oil pressure builds. This is a common issue across the M276 engine family. If ignored, chain slack can accelerate guide wear and potentially lead to timing misalignment. Some owners have reported that replacing tensioners alone may not cure the rattle if the VVT pins are already worn.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace hydraulic tensioners, install check valves per Mercedes TSB
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early when rattle first appears

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chains, tensioners, guides, camshaft sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: If rattle has persisted and chain stretch is confirmed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine swap with upgraded tensioners and timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If timing failure has caused valve damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2012-2020 SL 350, 400 or 450 is worth approximately £15,000-£40,000 depending on mileage, condition and specification. The R231 SL retains strong values for well-maintained examples, making replacement a justifiable investment for owners.
problems.recommendation: If your SL 350, 400 or 450 exhibits a rattling noise on cold start, act immediately. The M276's timing chain tensioners are a known weak point. Specialist tensioner replacement at £800-£1,300 is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. If the chain has stretched or jumped timing, a full rebuilt M276 engine with upgraded tensioners and timing components is the only safe option.

problems.group: M276 Oil Cooler Seal & Oil Leak Issues
problems.h4: M276 Oil Cooler Seal & Oil Leak Issues - The V6's Age-Related Weakness
problems.rootCause: The seals and gaskets for the engine oil cooler, located in the "V" of the engine, become brittle and fail due to heat cycling, causing oil to leak out. The front upper timing covers are another common source of oil leaks on the M276, which can lead to decreased oil levels and potential engine damage. Oil leaks can also affect wiring harnesses and, if they reach the ECU plug, can cause ECU failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil cooler seals, flush system, inspect for contamination
repairOptions.longevity: If caught early with no other damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace front upper timing cover gaskets, clean oil seepage
repairOptions.longevity: If oil leaks are from timing covers

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine swap with upgraded seals and gaskets, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If oil loss has caused internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - a typical R231 SL is worth £15,000-£40,000.
problems.recommendation: Oil leaks on the M276 are common with age but not usually urgent unless they are heavy. If you notice oil in the V of the engine or oil leaking onto wiring harnesses, have the oil cooler seals and timing covers inspected immediately. Specialist replacement at £700-£1,400 is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. Use only OEM Mercedes-Benz gaskets and seals for these engines.

problems.group: M276 Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves
problems.h4: M276 Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves - The Direct Injection Challenge
problems.rootCause: Direct injection engines like the M276 are prone to carbon buildup on intake valves because fuel is injected directly into the combustion chamber, bypassing the intake valves. Over time, carbon deposits accumulate on the valves, causing rough idle, reduced power, and poor fuel economy.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove intake manifold, walnut blast intake valves
repairOptions.longevity: If rough idle or misfires occur

repairOptions.longevity: If carbon buildup has caused valve damage

problems.recommendation: Carbon buildup is a known issue on all direct injection engines. If your SL 350, 400 or 450 experiences rough idle or reduced power, have the intake valves inspected.
